segments.speaker: Charlie
segments.text: Hey Lisa, I got your email with a meeting summary from Otter and I was curious about how it works. Have you been using it a lot for your meetings?

segments.speaker: Lisa
segments.text: Yeah, I started using Otter a few months ago. And it saved me a lot of time from taking manual notes. It also helps me find answers from previous meetings and even write follow up emails.

segments.speaker: Charlie
segments.text: Wow, really? Can you show me how it works?

segments.speaker: Lisa
segments.text: Sure. So this is Otter AI Chat. I can ask questions across all the conversations I've recorded with Otter, including meetings and voice memos. I can also use Otter AI Chat within a specific meeting to ask questions about just that meeting, like grouping ideas into themes from a brainstorm call.

segments.speaker: Charlie
segments.text: That sounds useful. And does Otter also summarize meetings automatically?

segments.speaker: Lisa
segments.text: Yes, exactly. Here on the conversation page, you can switch between the summary and transcript views. The summary view shows you the key topics in a meeting so you don't have to read through the full transcript. It also automatically generates action items and a more detailed outline which you can easily share with other people.  On the transcript view, you can see the full conversation and replay the audio recording. If Otter didn't transcribe a word or identify someone correctly, you can also edit both of those, which helps Otter improve.

segments.speaker: Charlie
segments.text: This is great. I can't wait to try it for my own meetings. So how do I tell Otter which meetings to record?

segments.speaker: Lisa
segments.text: Otter works by joining meetings on your calendar. It looks for events with a link from Zoom, Google Meet or Microsoft Teams. I have OtterPilot join most of my online meetings. And you can also toggle OtterPilot on and off depending on the meeting. I usually check which meetings Otter will join at the start of the week.

segments.speaker: Charlie
segments.text: Okay, got it and what happens when OtterPilot joins the meeting?

segments.speaker: Lisa
segments.text: When the meeting starts, your OtterPilot will appear as a participant in the meeting. In your case, it will be called Charlie's OtterPilot. During the meeting, you will get live notes along with automatic screenshots of screen shares. You can highlight and comment in the notes to quickly capture any thoughts or follow ups. And then after the meeting, you will see the meeting summary and action items.

segments.speaker: Charlie
segments.text: That'll be a time saver for sure. How do I share these notes with my teammates?

segments.speaker: Lisa
segments.text: There are a couple different ways you can share. If you go to your account settings, under the meeting tab, you can set up your default sharing setting. You can choose to share notes with calendar guests by default, with just people on your team, or you can keep the notes private. For every conversation, you can also choose who to share to by clicking the Share button on the top right corner.

segments.speaker: Charlie
segments.text: Okay, that makes sense. I do have a lot of recurring meetings as well. Is there a way I can put notes from the same meeting in one place?

segments.speaker: Lisa
segments.text: Yes, you can use Otter channels to organize your recurring meetings. Here in the left navigation bar, you can create a new Otter channel, decide if you want to make it a private or public channel in your workspace, and then invite other people into the channel. Then you can connect this channel to a recurring meeting on the calendar panel. And now all the notes for that recurring meeting will go into the same channel.

segments.speaker: Charlie
segments.text: That's terrific. So I don't have to scroll all the way back to find the notes from last week's meeting when I'm preparing for this week. By the way, you mentioned that Otter can join online meetings. What about in person meetings?

segments.speaker: Lisa
segments.text: Yes, for in person meetings. You can use Otter in your web browser or the mobile app on your iPhone or Android phone. When the meeting starts, just tap on the record button in Otter and as long as everyone's close enough to the microphone, Otter will take notes for you the same way.

segments.speaker: Charlie
segments.text: Perfect. I'll try out Otter for my meeting this afternoon. Thanks. Thanks.

segments.speaker: Lisa
segments.text: Yeah, anytime. Let me know what you think.
